task.description:
Hard gate: idiomatic style, scope creep, and decision-record consistency for ISS-0113/ISS-0423's fix. This change is test-infrastructure-only (no production code path touched) and has already been through: CODE-DESIGNER's original design (PASS at CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR), a real implementation FAIL at ELIXIR-DEV that traced a genuine 4th failure mechanism (a mid-test Sandbox.mode/2 call discarding a data-holding connection under async:true), a CODE-DESIGNER rework that removed the broken mechanism entirely and was independently regated by CODE-DESIGN-VALIDATOR (2 real test runs, different seeds, 38/38 clean both times), and an ELIXIR-DEV sign-off (a THIRD independent test run, different seed again, also 38/38 clean).

Your job:
1. Read lib/letflow/design/iss0113-tenant-fixture-sandbox-restore-opt-in.md's section 9 (the normative, corrected mechanism) and confirm the reasoning holds up to your own scrutiny -- is relying on provisioned_tenant!/1's existing, unconditional Sandbox.mode(:auto) call (rather than adding new sandbox-management code) a genuinely idiomatic OTP/Ecto testing pattern for this codebase, or does it introduce any fragility (e.g. does it depend on call ORDER within provisioned_tenant!/1 in a way that a future edit to that function could silently break, without anything catching it)?
2. Confirm this change does not touch lib/letflow/process_instance.ex, instance_supervisor.ex, or any supervision-tree file (it shouldn't -- test-only).
3. Confirm no scope creep: read the actual diff (git diff origin/main -- test/support/tenant_fixture.ex test/letflow/secrets_test.exs test/letflow/webhooks_test.exs) and confirm it matches exactly what the design's section 8/9.6 calls for -- nothing extra.
4. Confirm consistency with existing decision records: does this change contradict anything in docs/migration/decisions/0009-test-parallel-pool-sizing.md (it should not -- the design's own section 6 already reconciles this, confirm that reconciliation is sound) or any other decision record you're aware of?
5. Check whether the design's own stated risk (design section 9, if a future edit to provisioned_tenant!/1 reorders the :auto call or adds a new mid-function Sandbox.mode/2 call, this fix could silently break again) is adequately guarded against -- is there a comment/moduledoc warning at the right place in tenant_fixture.ex to prevent a future editor from reintroducing the exact defect this run found and reverted? If not, this may be worth a MINOR finding (not necessarily a BLOCKER) recommending one, though the moduledoc note already added should be checked first before assuming it's missing.
6. State your verdict plainly.
acceptance_criteria: Design section 9's mechanism confirmed idiomatically sound, or specific concerns named
Confirmed the actual diff matches the design's own stated scope exactly, no extras
Confirmed no contradiction with decision 0009 or other decision records
Checked whether a guard/comment exists against future reintroduction of the exact defect this run found and reverted -- named as present or missing
